reasons.StaleParent: Another version became the family's latest after this one was prepared. Start again from the new latest.

reasons.VERSION_NOT_APPROVED: The version was no longer approved.
reasons.NONCE_CONSUMED: Another transaction used this write's slot, so it can never be mined. Approve again to retry.
reasons.TX_REVERTED: The transaction was mined but the registry refused it.
reasons.SEND_REJECTED: The node refused the transaction before sending it; nothing was broadcast.
reasons.REPLACEMENT_REJECTED: A higher-fee replacement was refused; the original transaction is still pending.
reasons.ISSUER_BLOCKED: Waiting: an earlier write with an unknown outcome must be settled first.
reasons.SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN: The worker stopped while sending. The outcome is being read from the chain; nothing is resent.
reasons.TX_NOT_FOUND: The node no longer knows the transaction. The outcome is being read from the chain; nothing is resent.
reasons.NO_RPC_ANSWER: The node did not answer the send. The outcome is being read from the chain; nothing is resent.
reasons.NONCE_TOO_LOW: The node says this slot is already used. The outcome is being read from the chain.
reasons.RPC_ERROR: The node answered with an unexpected error. The outcome is being read from the chain; nothing is resent.
reasons.RECORD_MISMATCH: The record on chain does not match what was sent. A person must look at this.
reasons.CANNOT_REPLACE: The pending transaction could not be replaced.
reasons.NotIssuer: The issuer key is not registered with the registry.
reasons.STAMP_CHECK: The stamped copy did not pass its check against the original and the final record, so nothing was stored or sent.
reasons.ANCHOR_ONLY: This version is signed or edit-protected, so it is never stamped.
reasons.COPY_NEEDS_LIVE: A distribution copy is anchored only in Live mode.
reasons.CopyExists: The original already has a distribution copy on chain, made from another file.
reasons.RevocationExists: A revocation is already on chain for this record, pending or in effect.
reasons.KIND_UNSUPPORTED: The worker does not send this kind of write.

reasons.ORIGINAL_RECORD_MISMATCH: The original’s record on chain is not this version’s, or is not final yet.

anchoring.completeCopy: Complete: the stamped distribution copy is anchored too. Hand recipients this copy; its metadata names its own record.
anchoring.completeCertificate: Complete. This report is signed or protected against editing, so it was anchored as issued. Hand recipients the report as issued together with its verification certificate.
anchoring.copyPending: The original is anchored. Its distribution copy is being stamped, checked and anchored.
anchoring.copyFailed: The original is anchored, but its distribution copy was not. See the reason below.
anchoring.certificatePending: Anchored as issued. The verification certificate is being prepared.
anchoring.retryBody: The worker stamps the original again (or reuses a copy already checked) and anchors it from the issuer key. The version's approval covers its copy.

ots.title: Bitcoin timestamp
ots.what: A second, independent timestamp of the manifest hash, on Bitcoin through OpenTimestamps. It does not rest on this firm's registry or on the chain the report is anchored on.
ots.none: Not submitted yet. The OpenTimestamps job submits each version once its anchor is final.
ots.pending: Waiting for Bitcoin: submitted {when} (UTC) to {count} calendars. Bitcoin usually confirms within a few hours.
ots.complete: In Bitcoin block {height}, mined about {when} (UTC). The manifest hash existed by then.
ots.broken: This proof does not lead to the block it names ({reason}). It shows no time, and a person must look at it (docs/runbooks/opentimestamps.md).

reasons.CALENDARS_UNREACHABLE: The calendars could not be reached on the last try.
reasons.BITCOIN_UNREADABLE: The block explorers could not be read on the last try.
reasons.BITCOIN_DISAGREE: The two block explorers gave different blocks on the last try.
reasons.BITCOIN_BAD_HEADER: The block explorers gave a block without Bitcoin's proof of work.

verify.title: Verify an audit report
verify.intro: Choose or drop a PDF. It is checked here, in your browser, and never uploaded: the page computes the file's fingerprint and reads the public registry directly. For a registered report it also asks the issuer's server for its Bitcoin timestamp, by the report's public manifest fingerprint.
verify.checksAgainst: Checked against the registry {contract} on {network}, read through two endpoints whose answers must agree.
verify.disclaimer: Records on a public test network are prototype evidence, not a legally binding record.
verify.notConfigured: The verifier is not configured on this server.

setupRefusal.NETWORK_INVALID: VERIFY_NETWORK must be sepolia or local.
setupRefusal.DEPLOYMENT_UNAVAILABLE: The registry's deployment record is missing or does not match this build.
setupRefusal.RPC_URLS_MISSING: VERIFY_RPC_URL_1 and VERIFY_RPC_URL_2 must both be set.
setupRefusal.RPC_URLS_INVALID: The verifier's RPC endpoints must be https URLs without credentials.
setupRefusal.RPC_URLS_NOT_INDEPENDENT: The verifier's two RPC endpoints must be on different hosts.

AUTHENTIC_SUPERSEDED.title: Authentic, superseded
AUTHENTIC_SUPERSEDED.body: This file is byte for byte the file the issuer anchored, but the issuer has since anchored version {latest} of this report. Rely on the latest version.

REVOKED.title: Revoked
REVOKED.body: This file was anchored by the issuer and later revoked. Do not rely on it.

REVOCATION_PENDING.title: Being withdrawn
REVOCATION_PENDING.body: This file is byte for byte the file the issuer anchored, but the issuer has asked to withdraw it. The withdrawal takes effect on {when} unless the registry’s owner cancels it first. Do not rely on it without asking the issuer.

ALTERED_OPINION_CHANGED.title: Altered: the opinion differs
ALTERED_OPINION_CHANGED.body: This is not the file the issuer anchored. It refers to an anchored report, but the audit opinion in it does not match that report's opinion. This is strong evidence that the opinion was edited.

ALTERED_OPINION_APPEARS_UNCHANGED.title: Not the registered file; the opinion text matches
ALTERED_OPINION_APPEARS_UNCHANGED.body: This is not the file the issuer anchored. It refers to an anchored report, and the opinion text in it matches that report's opinion. That shows only that the opinion wording is the same: anything else in the file may have changed. Ask the issuer for the registered file.

ALTERED_OPINION_NOT_CHECKABLE.title: Not the registered file; the opinion could not be checked
ALTERED_OPINION_NOT_CHECKABLE.body: This is not the file the issuer anchored. It refers to an anchored report, but the opinion could not be found in its text, so it could not be compared.

UNKNOWN_REGISTRY.title: Refers to another registry
UNKNOWN_REGISTRY.body: This file refers to a record on chain {chainId} at {contract}, which this verifier does not check. Nothing has been verified.

CANNOT_VERIFY.title: Cannot verify right now
CANNOT_VERIFY.body: No verdict was reached. {reason} Try again later.

notRegistered.NO_REFERENCE: No report anchored in this registry is this exact file, and the file carries no anchor reference. This says nothing either way about where the file came from.
notRegistered.REFERENCE_UNREADABLE: No report anchored in this registry is this exact file. The file carries an anchor reference, but it is not well formed.
notRegistered.NAMES_UNKNOWN_RECORD: No report anchored in this registry is this exact file. The file refers to a record that this registry does not hold.
notRegistered.PDF_UNREADABLE: No report anchored in this registry is this exact file, and the file could not be read as a PDF to look for an anchor reference.

revocation.title: Revocation
revocation.intro: A revocation withdraws this version on chain: anyone who checks it, or a copy of it, is told it was revoked. An admin asks for it, and an approver who is someone else approves. The registry then waits out a delay before it takes effect, during which only the registry’s owner can cancel it. Once in effect, it cannot be undone.
revocation.adminOnly: Only an admin can ask for a version to be revoked.
revocation.noteHint: Why, for the firm’s records. It is kept encrypted and never sent to the chain.
revocation.confirmLabel: Type the engagement reference, {ref}, to confirm
revocation.requestTitle: Ask for version {version} to be revoked?
revocation.requestBody: An approver who is someone else must approve the request before anything is sent. Once on chain, the revocation takes effect after the registry’s delay, and from then on it cannot be undone.
revocation.requested: {who} asked on {when} UTC for this version to be revoked.
revocation.waitingApprover: Waiting for an approver who is someone else.
revocation.approveBody: The revocation is written to the journal and sent to the chain. Once its block is final, the registry’s delay runs; when it ends, the verifier reports this version, and every copy of it, as revoked, and that cannot be undone. Until then only the registry’s owner can cancel it.
revocation.approveBodyDryRun: Dry run: the revocation is simulated against the registry and the result recorded. Nothing is sent, and the request waits for approval again.
revocation.rejectBody: The version stays as it is. An admin can ask again.
revocation.withdrawBody: The version stays as it is.
revocation.queued: Approved by {who}. The revocation is in the journal; once its block is final, the registry’s delay runs before it takes effect.
revocation.scheduled: On chain: takes effect on {when} UTC, unless the registry’s owner cancels it first. Until then the verifier says this version is being withdrawn.
revocation.cancelled: The registry’s owner cancelled this revocation on chain before it took effect. The version stands; an admin can ask again.
revocation.cancelledOn: cancelled by the registry’s owner; found {when} UTC

now.title: The chain, re-derived now
now.intact: Every one of the {count} events hashes to the next. The newest event’s hash:

nightly.title: The nightly check
nightly.neverRun: The nightly check has never run. Schedule `npm run audit:check` once a day.
nightly.intact: Last run {when} UTC: intact, {count} events, and nothing earlier was cut or rewritten.
nightly.heads: Held to {count, plural, one {# head} other {# heads}} of this log on chain; the latest was written {when} UTC.
nightly.noHeads: No head of this log is on chain yet: one is written after a check once anchoring is live.
nightly.stale: The nightly check last ran {when} UTC, more than a day and a half ago. It has stopped running.
nightly.how: Each night every hash is re-derived, and the chain is held to the last intact check: it may only have grown, and the event that was its head must still be there, unchanged. The check also writes the log’s latest hash to the registry, and every head there must still be in the log, so whoever owns the database cannot rewrite the log’s past and its checks together.

watch.title: The registry watch
watch.neverRun: The registry watch has never run. Until it does, nothing notices a write by the firm’s issuer keys that the console did not make. Schedule `npm run watch:registry` every ten minutes.
watch.current: Read the chain up to finalized block {block}, at {when} UTC.
watch.stale: The registry watch last ran at {when} UTC. It should run every ten minutes: check its schedule.
watch.none: Every write by the firm’s issuer keys that it has read is in the journal.
watch.open: {count, plural, one {# write} other {# writes}} on chain by the firm’s issuer keys that the console did not make. Treat the key as stolen until you know otherwise.
watch.deadline: Takes effect {when} UTC, unless the registry’s owner cancels it before then (docs/runbooks/stolen-issuer-key.md).
watch.more: {count, plural, one {# more is} other {# more are}} not shown.
watch.reviewBody: Do this once someone has looked into it: the owner cancelled the revocation, the key was retired, or the write was the firm’s own and lost from the journal. It stays in the audit log.
watch.how: The watch runs outside the app (`npm run watch:registry`). It reads every anchor and revocation by the firm’s issuer keys up to the finalized block, and reports each whose transaction no journal row holds. It exits with an error while any write here is open.

reasons.SEQ_GAP: an event is missing or out of order
reasons.PREV_HASH_MISMATCH: it does not link to the event before it
reasons.HASH_MISMATCH: its contents do not match its hash
reasons.TRUNCATED: events that an earlier check saw are gone
reasons.REWRITTEN: an event that an earlier check saw has been replaced
reasons.ANCHORED_HEAD_MISSING: a head of this log written on chain is no longer in it: the log was rewritten or cut since
reasons.CHAIN_UNREADABLE: the chain could not be read, so the log could not be held to its heads there

superseded.noReport: This message carries no report, no opinion and no figures.

revoked.subject: {firm}: version {version} of the audit report for {client} is withdrawn
revoked.body: {firm} has withdrawn version {version} of the audit report for {client} (period ending {periodEnd}, engagement {engagementRef}). Do not rely on any copy of that version.
revoked.latest: The report’s latest record, read from the public chain: {latestUrl}
revoked.verify: To check a copy you hold, open {verifyUrl} and choose the file. It is checked in your browser and never uploaded.
revoked.noReport: This message carries no report, no opinion and no figures.
revoked.prototype: Prototype: records on a public test network are prototype evidence, not a legally binding record.

recipients.title: Recipients
recipients.intro: People who hold a copy of this report, such as a lender, a regulator or a shareholder. When a newer version supersedes it, each is emailed a link to the latest version’s record: never the report, the opinion or a figure. They ask the firm for the report itself.
recipients.name: Name
recipients.removeBody: They will not be told about later versions, and anything not yet sent to them is cancelled.

lastRevoked.PENDING: Withdrawal of version {version}: waiting to be sent
lastRevoked.FAILED: Withdrawal of version {version}: could not be sent
